entries.title: Policy feedback and media framing of crime victims
entries.abstract: Drawing on framing theory and the social construction of target populations, this study examines whether and how landmark legislation is associated with shifts in media framing of the populations it targets. We examine this question through the Crime Victims’ Rights Act of 2004 (CVRA), landmark legislation that significantly changed the way the legal process understood victims. By expanding victims’ participatory rights in the prosecution of those who harmed them, it designated victims as deserving a voice in the process and institutionalised the fact that the victim’s experience mattered for the fair provision of justice. entries.title: Bureaucratic behavior in the implementation of freedom of information laws: evidence from a field experiment in Belgian municipalities
entries.abstract: Abstract Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are widely adopted to promote transparency, yet their implementation diverges from formal legal expectations. This article examines how variations in FOI requests shape administrative responses and what these patterns reveal about bureaucratic behavior in municipal administrations. Drawing on a randomized field experiment across Belgian municipalities, the study analyzes how public officials respond to identical FOI requests varying by requester identity and legal framing. The findings show that responsiveness is not neutral but varies systematically across request characteristics and contexts. entries.title: Bureaucratic behavior in the implementation of freedom of information laws: evidence from a field experiment in Belgian municipalities
entries.abstract: Abstract Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are widely adopted to promote transparency, yet their implementation diverges from formal legal expectations. This article examines how variations in FOI requests shape administrative responses and what these patterns reveal about bureaucratic behavior in municipal administrations. Drawing on a randomized field experiment across Belgian municipalities, the study analyzes how public officials respond to identical FOI requests varying by requester identity and legal framing. The findings show that responsiveness is not neutral but varies systematically across request characteristics and contexts. Ordinary citizens receive higher disclosure rates than institutional or advocacy actors, and invoking FOI law increases compliance for some requesters while reducing it for others.
